leads.candidate: The McKenna Cottonwoods (Eastern Cottonwood duo), Notre-Dame-des-Neiges Cemetery, a little off block ND 1-3967, in front of headstone 893
leads.reason: Held back at merge, 2026-09-10. montroyal.montreal.ca/arbre-remarquable/peuplier-deltoide-1 gives no coordinate at all, only 'un peu a l'ecart des alignements d'arbres de l'ilot ND 1-3967, arbre portant l'etiquette 893' (checked by refetching the source page directly). The verify pass's draft had filled the coordinate field with the cemetery's main-entrance point, identical to the six-decimal-place coordinate already published as mtl_004 (the Wide Pine at the Cemetery Gate, a different species standing at a different spot in the grounds). Publishing that would send a reader to a pine, not these poplars, exactly the wrong-location failure hard rule 2 exists to prevent; passcheck's coordinate-collision check caught it before merge. Existence, species and age are otherwise solid, corroborated by two Ville de Montreal pages (the individual entry and the cemetery's own landscape overview). Ships as soon as someone can place block ND 1-3967 on a cemetery section map.

leads.candidate: Peuplier deltoide (Eastern Cottonwood), Parc du Mont-Royal, along Chemin Olmsted (distinct from the verified McKenna Cottonwoods duo at Notre-Dame-des-Neiges, mtl_009)
leads.reason: montroyal.montreal.ca/arbre-remarquable/peuplier-deltoide-0. Different property (Parc du Mont-Royal, Ville-Marie borough) and different story from the cemetery duo: this one stands in a tree alignment along the Chemin Olmsted, on a steep-pitched site, possibly planted to replace a lost tree in Olmsted's original row rather than naturally grown. DBH 170 cm (roughly 534 cm girth), estimated 90 years, rooted spectacularly on a steep slope. Only one source read this pass (the register page itself); no second source sought yet. A clean candidate for a future pass, and it would join the existing Mont-Royal cluster (mtl_002, mtl_005) rather than needing its own note.

leads.candidate: Arbre de Katsura and Metasequoia de Chine (dawn redwood), both at Universite McGill, planted 1965 by botany professor Darnley Gibbs at the opening of the Stewart Biological Sciences pavilion
leads.reason: montroyal.montreal.ca/arbre-remarquable/arbre-de-katsura and /metasequoia-de-chine. Both genuinely remarkable (the Katsura is three-trunked and among the largest of its species in the Montreal region; the dawn redwood is a 'living fossil' species not known alive until 1941 and this specimen is probably the largest of its species in Quebec). NOT verified/shipped this pass because the source describes their site as 'l'interieur de la cour du pavillon Stewart Biological Sciences... cour restreinte encadree de hauts edifices' (the interior of the Stewart Biological Sciences building's courtyard, a restricted courtyard framed by tall buildings), and a search this pass could not confirm whether that courtyard is open, publicly walkable campus ground (like mtl_001's Chancellor Day Hall lawn) or an enclosed space effectively requiring building access. Needs a targeted access check (OSM tags, a campus map, or a McGill facilities page) before it can ship per hard rule 10's 'can they get in without asking anyone's permission' test. If confirmed open, both are strong candidates and could ship together as a short addition to the McGill cluster.

leads.candidate: Other named Mont-Royal / McGill remarkable trees on montroyal.montreal.ca not reached this pass
leads.reason: The site's search index (montroyal.montreal.ca/recherche?texte=Arbre+remarquable) lists more individually documented specimens beyond what this and the 2026-08-16 pass have verified: yellowwood (virgilier-bois-jaune), two yellow-flowered horse chestnuts (marronnier-fleurs-jaunes, marronnier-fleurs-jaunes-0), a European spindle tree (fusain-d'europe), plus the earlier pass's unreached list (Katsura tree companion the late black cherry near mtl_008, more sugar/silver maples, dawn redwoods elsewhere, tulip tree companions, black walnut, bitternut and shagbark hickory, white ash, paper birch, western catalpa, phellodendron, more deltoid poplars, Kentucky coffeetree at both Notre-Dame-des-Neiges and College Notre-Dame). At least 6 pages of search results as of 2026-08-16; register-style individual pages with DBH already exist for most, so verification is closer to confirm-and-pin than research-from-zero. High-value source for a future pass.

leads.candidate: Six Mount Royal Cemetery trees on an ArcGIS layer named 'Arbres remarquables' (owner cimetiereonline): silver maple, honey locust, Japanese yew, two Eastern cottonwoods, European black pine, all within 800m on the Mount Royal slope
leads.reason: 2026-09-12: probed from an earlier arcgis-register-sweep hit. NOT a licensed register (no licence statement found on the ArcGIS item) and carries only species and coordinates, no name, age or girth, so it cannot be imported and does not meet the two-source verification bar on its own. Matches the same silver maple, honey locust, black pine and one cottonwood already published (mtl_004, mtl_006, mtl_007, part of mtl_009's pair) and the yew already published as mtl_003, so this ArcGIS layer is mostly corroboration of what montroyal.montreal.ca already gave us rather than new supply. The one net-new point is a second, distinct Japanese yew and a second cottonwood pair member at slightly different coordinates from the published entries; worth a targeted montroyal.montreal.ca search next time (see the 'second Japanese yew' lead above) rather than trusting this layer's coordinates directly. Full detail in data/research/montreal-register-candidates.json.

blocked.candidate: Frene rouge (Red Ash, Fraxinus pennsylvanica), Notre-Dame-des-Neiges Cemetery, in front of the Resurrection Chapel, lot B74-87
blocked.reason: DEAD. Confirmed via the source's own page, which now redirects from /arbre-remarquable/frene-rouge to /arbre-remarquable/frene-rouge-disparu ('vanished'): 'cet arbre a du etre abattu en 2025 du aux dommages causes par l'agrile du frene' (had to be felled in 2025 due to emerald ash borer damage). This was the 7th of the cemetery's originally-designated 7 remarkable trees; its removal is exactly why the unlicensed ArcGIS lead layer's 6 points match only 6 of the cemetery's originally 7 named species. Never ship. Matches the brief's specific warning about ash trees needing a post-2015 recency check.
